method: rule-based v1 (water balance + heat stress + root zone soil wetness)

crops.name: Olive
crops.notes: Very drought tolerant once established, long-term investment (3-5 years before full yield).

crops.name: Barley
crops.notes: More drought tolerant than wheat and harvested earlier, so it escapes some of the late heat.

crops.name: Lentil
crops.notes: Short cycle legume, sensitive to heat at flowering.

crops.name: Faba bean
crops.notes: Needs more water than other legumes, sensitive to heat at flowering.

crops.name: Chickpea
crops.notes: Fixes nitrogen, good in rotation after cereals. High value per kg.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.notes: Main cereal of the region. Hurt by dry springs and heat during grain filling (Apr - May).

crops.name: Tomato (open field)
crops.notes: High income but needs full irrigation, so it depends on water access.

rotations.name: Wheat after wheat
rotations.why: This is the most common practice in the region today. It is the baseline the other strategies are compared with.
benefits: Known market, guaranteed reference price and simple to manage
Farmers already have the seeds, equipment and experience
risks: Wheat is the crop most hurt by spring heat and dry seasons in the NASA data
Growing the same cereal every year builds up pests and root diseases (Hessian fly, root rot) and depletes soil nitrogen
Needs more nitrogen fertiliser every year
gaps: Actual fertiliser use and yields on each farm
evidence: Replayed on the real 2011-2025 seasons, it would have lost money in 9 of 15 seasons.
Climate fit 68/100 today, 69/100 with the 1991-2005 climate.
In the driest recent season (2022-2023), its crops score 48/100.
Needs about 198 mm of extra water per season to reach full yield (1980 m³/ha).

rotations.name: Wheat → Chickpea
rotations.why: Chickpea is a legume that fixes nitrogen from the air and is sown in late winter, after the wettest months, so it uses rain that wheat cannot.
benefits: Leaves nitrogen in the soil for the next wheat crop, so less fertiliser
Breaks the cereal disease and pest cycle
High value per kg, a second source of income
risks: Chickpea is sensitive to heat in May and to ascochyta blight in wet springs
Harvest is more labour intensive, prices vary more than wheat
gaps: Disease pressure in the farmer's area
evidence: Replayed on the real 2011-2025 seasons, it would have lost money in 5.5 of 15 seasons (wheat after wheat: 9).
Climate fit 68/100 today, 69/100 with the 1991-2005 climate.
In the driest recent season (2022-2023), its crops score 49/100 (wheat after wheat: 48).
Needs about 171 mm of extra water per season to reach full yield (1710 m³/ha).
Income includes about 500 MAD/ha saved on nitrogen fertiliser for the cereal that follows the legume (estimate).

rotations.name: Barley → Faba bean
rotations.why: Barley is the most drought tolerant cereal and is harvested before the late spring heat. Faba bean is a legume that fixes a lot of nitrogen and its residues feed livestock.
benefits: The most resilient option in dry seasons according to the NASA data
Strong nitrogen fixation and organic matter from faba residues
Both crops can be used as forage, useful for farms with sheep or cattle
risks: Barley earns less per tonne than wheat
Faba bean needs more water than other legumes and is sensitive to heat at flowering
gaps: Whether the farm has livestock or a forage market nearby
Soil type: faba bean does poorly on very shallow soils
evidence: Replayed on the real 2011-2025 seasons, it would have lost money in 1 of 15 seasons (wheat after wheat: 9).
Climate fit 76/100 today, 75/100 with the 1991-2005 climate.
In the driest recent season (2022-2023), its crops score 60/100 (wheat after wheat: 48).
Needs about 142 mm of extra water per season to reach full yield (1420 m³/ha).
Income includes about 500 MAD/ha saved on nitrogen fertiliser for the cereal that follows the legume (estimate).

rotations.name: Wheat → Lentil → Barley
rotations.why: A three-year rotation spreads the risk across three crops with different calendars and keeps wheat only one year in three.
benefits: Longest break in the cereal pest cycle
Lentil fixes nitrogen and has a short cycle that escapes part of the spring heat
Diversified income: no single crop failure ruins the farm
risks: More complex to plan: three seed types and harvest periods
Lentil is sensitive to heat at flowering (March - April)
gaps: Access to lentil seeds and buyers
evidence: Replayed on the real 2011-2025 seasons, it would have lost money in 4.7 of 15 seasons (wheat after wheat: 9).
Climate fit 74/100 today, 74/100 with the 1991-2005 climate.
In the driest recent season (2022-2023), its crops score 56/100 (wheat after wheat: 48).
Needs about 144 mm of extra water per season to reach full yield (1440 m³/ha).
Income includes about 500 MAD/ha saved on nitrogen fertiliser for the cereal that follows the legume (estimate).
